title: instagram
description: Scrapes posts, and optionally comments, from a public Instagram profile or hashtag. A date range is a window the run must COVER, not merely filter to: with start_date/end_date and no max_posts, the run collects every post in the range and reports whether it managed to cover it. Needs an authenticated session, forwarded to the Worker as IG_SESSION.

target.description: A profile ('nasa', or an instagram.com/... URL) or a hashtag ('#space' or 'space' when mode is hashtag).

mode.description: What the target names. Defaults to 'profile'. A hashtag feed is RANKED, not chronological (top posts first, then recent), so a date range over one can only filter what it is served - it cannot page backwards to cover a period the way a profile can.

max_posts.description: Cap on posts returned. OMIT IT when using a date range on a profile: the range is then the stopping condition, and a count here would cut the window short.

start_date.description: Only posts at or after this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means midnight.

end_date.description: Only posts at or before this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means end of day.

collect_comments.description: Also collect each post's comments and replies. Considerably slower. Defaults to false.

analyse.description: Also produce an AI analysis and report (text, PDF and an HTML dashboard) alongside the data. Defaults to true. Costs two Claude calls; the scrape itself is unaffected either way.

ai_prompt.description: Your own analysis instructions, e.g. 'focus on complaints about delivery times'. Added to the built-in brief rather than replacing it, so the report keeps its structure and always renders.
